source.raw_extract:
ROLLING PROCESS

Most financial aid applications are accepted and evaluated on a rolling basis. You can submit your financial aid application once you have applied for admission and always before the start of the program.
source.exact_deadline_wording: Most financial aid applications are accepted and evaluated on a rolling basis. You can submit your financial aid application once you have applied for admission and always before the start of the program.
source.notes: Provider states the process explicitly as rolling and gives no calendar date, so ROLLING is used and no date is invented. The bound is the programme start date, not a published closing date. Two official IE pages agree and do not conflict.

corroborating_sources.raw_extract:
DIRECT AWARDS

These merit-based awards are granted automatically upon admission—no separate financial aid application is required. All applicants are considered as part of the admissions process.

IE AWARDS

These awards are available to candidates across all master’s programs and may cover between 10% and 40% of tuition fees. All IE Awards require the submission of a financial aid application and are assessed based on both merit and financial need. The application deadline for IE Awards is the program start date.

IE FOUNDATION SCHOLARSHIPS

IE Foundation partners with a range of organizations to offer these scholarships and awards opportunities. Be sure to review the specific eligibility criteria, deadlines, and application requirements for each scholarship and award, as some may require submitting an additional, scholarship-specific essay in the “Additional Documentation” section of the IE Financial Aid Application.
corroborating_sources.supports: Consistent with the rolling statement on the how-to-apply page: Direct Awards need no separate application, IE Awards close on the programme start date, and individual IE Foundation Scholarships carry their own separate deadlines (which are not published on this page and were not resolved per scholarship).

records.title: UGC Junior Research Fellowship (JRF) and Research Associateship (RA) for Foreign Nationals
records.deadline_display: The applications are invited through circulation to Indian embassies/Indian missions abroad.

source.publisher: University Grants Commission, Government of India
source.as_of: XIth Plan Guidelines; no cycle year, edition date or application year is stated in the document.
source.raw_extract:
PROCEDURE FOR APPLYING FOR THE SCHEME:

The applications are invited through circulation to Indian embassies/Indian missions abroad. They will receive applications from eligible candidates and after due screening locally, will send them to the UGC for consideration. Foreign students from Asia, Africa and Latin America studying in India who have completed their master's degrees or doctoral degrees and desire to pursue research may send their applications through the university they propose to work with. The application will have to be endorsed by their respective embassies for consideration by the Commission.
source.exact_deadline_wording: The applications are invited through circulation to Indian embassies/Indian missions abroad.
source.notes: The official 25-page UGC guidelines for this exact scheme were downloaded and read in full (all pages extracted). They contain NO calendar application deadline of any kind. The only timing reference is an age-eligibility cut-off, not a deadline: "For Junior Research Fellowship (JRF): 35 years for male candidates as on 1 July of the year of application and 40 years for female candidates." Using that date would misreport an eligibility rule as an application deadline, so it was rejected. Because the guidelines neither state a rolling basis nor state recurring annual timing, ANNUAL and ROLLING were both refused as inferences. UNKNOWN is the truthful result. The PDF is the official document linked from UGC's live XI Plan Guidelines index as item 16 under "For Individual", titled "Junior Research Fellowship (JRF) and Research Associateship (RA) for Foreign Nationals".

field_mapping.deadline_display: The applications are invited through circulation to Indian embassies/Indian missions abroad.
field_mapping.note: No official calendar deadline exists to write. Timing is set by each Indian mission's own local call, which is not published by UGC.

rejected_sources.reason: Homepage carries no JRF/RA-for-foreign-nationals call. The official pages were read in full and state only that applications are open, plus a near-deadline rule for a different track ("The deadline for transfer applications depends on the applicant's desired start date."). shard_summary.note: No deadline_date was written for any record. Five records carry an explicit but past calendar deadline and are reported as expired_mismatch with the evidence date preserved only under withheld_deadline for traceability, never in deadline_date. One record (IE University) is ROLLING on the provider's explicit wording. Two records (UGC JRF/RA foreign nationals; Asian University for Women) publish no deadline at all and are UNKNOWN. No source disagreed with another source about the same deadline, so no CONFLICTING was recorded.
